messages.content: 关于论文《Mapping Languages and Demographics with Georeferenced Corpora》，Do they authors offer a hypothesis for why Twitter data makes better predictions about the inventory of languages used in each country?

claims.text: The paper reports that Twitter data makes better predictions about the inventory of languages used in each country.

In many cases the two corpora agree on which languages they predict to be used per country (Europe, parts of Africa with ground-truth, and South America), but Twitter provides a better representation of North America and Oceania.
The authors note that English and Spanish are very common on Twitter, so any country predominantly using these two languages will have a good representation by default.
The Discussion states that where corpora fail to represent all census languages, Twitter has fewer missing languages than the web-crawled corpus.
The paper notes there are more false positives in Twitter data than in web-crawled data, indicating more diverse language-speaking populations in some countries when relying on Twitter alone.

For the divergence between Twitter and web-crawled populations, the authors hypothesize that Twitter as a platform represents more wealthy populations, since Twitter data matches populations better when weighted by GDP and worse when weighted by internet-usage statistics, with an alternate interpretation that their Twitter collection is based on urban areas, which tend to have wealthier populations.
The authors state that more research is needed to distinguish between immigration, tourism, and business as alternate sources of false positive languages in digital data.

claims.text: 论文摘要指出，Twitter数据在预测各国所使用的语言清单方面表现更好。
讨论部分指出，在语料库未涵盖当地人口所使用的全部语言的国家中，Twitter缺失的语言更少。
论文指出，Twitter为北美和大洋洲提供了更好的代表性。
论文指出，英语和西班牙语在Twitter上非常普遍，因此任何主要使用这两种语言的国家默认就会得到较好的代表性。
论文提到，当人口数量按GDP加权时，Twitter数据与人口的匹配更好；作者认为这表明Twitter平台所代表的人群比一般网络抓取数据所代表的人群更富裕。
论文提出另一种解释：本文的Twitter收集基于城市地区，而城市地区往往拥有更富裕的人口。
论文指出，虽然不常见，但Twitter数据中的假阳性更多；在Twitter上，美国和加拿大、南非、法国、印度和澳大利亚也存在过度预测的语言。
论文表示，需要更多研究来区分移民、旅游和商业作为数字数据集中出现假阳性语言的其他来源。
论文发现Twitter与网络抓取数据模式在代表世界人口方面存在显著差异，并将其简单归因于来自Twitter和网页的数据很可能代表来自不同地点的人。

messages.content: 与《Unsupervised Question Answering for Fact-Checking》对比，分别说明两篇论文如何回答“Do they authors offer a hypothesis for why Twitter data makes better predictions about the inventory of languages used in each country?”与“How large is the FEVER dataset?”，并说明是否具有可比性。

claims.text: 《Unsupervised Question Answering for Fact-Checking》没有提出关于 Twitter 数据为何能更好预测各国语言清单的假设；该文仅在引言中提及 Twitter 作为需要信息核验的平台之一，且其模型从未使用 Twitter 数据。
《Mapping Languages and Demographics with Georeferenced Corpora》报告“Twitter 数据能更好地预测每个国家所用语言的清单”，但所给证据仅呈现该结论，未给出解释性假设。
该文还发现两种语料相关性极低（r=0.05），表明网络抓取数据与 Twitter 数据代表不同人群；按 GDP 调整后，Twitter 数据与人口的相关性由 r=0.39 升至 r=0.60。
《Unsupervised Question Answering for Fact-Checking》称 FEVER 是最大的数据集，包含约 185k 条 claim，语料来自 5.4M 篇 Wikipedia 文章，claim 被标注为 SUPPORTS、REFUTES 或 NOT ENOUGH INFO。
该文将 FEVER 数据集转换为 Cloze 任务，并在其变换后的开发集和测试集上分别取得 80.2% 与 80.25% 的标签准确率。
所给《Mapping Languages and Demographics with Georeferenced Corpora》的证据中未出现 FEVER 数据集规模的信息。
两篇论文在这两个问题上不可直接比较：Twitter 语言清单结论只出现在地理参照语料研究中，而 FEVER 规模只由事实核查论文给出，各自证据中缺乏对应项。
